record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: To what extent does increasing stakeholder and data diversity through federated training improve model fairness, and how do required differential privacy mechanisms affect the fairness, performance, and diversity gains of such federated training?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a central model is trained collaboratively over $K$ clients, where client $k$ holds a local dataset $D_k$ drawn from a client-specific distribution $\mathcal{P}_k$ over an input–output space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$, with each example additionally carrying a sensitive attribute $a\in\mathcal{A}$ (e.g., a demographic group). Let $\mathcal{D}=\bigcup_k D_k$ denote the aggregated training distribution and let $\mathrm{Div}(\{\mathcal{P}_k\})$ be a measure of stakeholder/data diversity (for instance, the average pairwise total variation distance between the $\mathcal{P}_k$ or the coverage of $\mathcal{A}$ across clients). Let $h_\theta:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ be the trained global model, and define:
- a performance functional $U(h_\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{P}^\star}[\ell(h_\theta(x),y)]$ against a target distribution $\mathcal{P}^\star$;
- a group-fairness functional $F(h_\theta)$, such as the maximum gap in true-positive rates, demographic parity, or accuracy across values of $a$.

Assume the federated training protocol satisfies $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy with respect to either record-level or client-level adjacency, implemented via gradient clipping at norm $C$ and Gaussian noise of scale $\sigma$ at the aggregation step.

Provide a rigorous quantitative analysis of the following:

(a) Establish, as a function of $\mathrm{Div}(\{\mathcal{P}_k\})$, upper and lower bounds on the achievable fairness $F(h_\theta)$ when no privacy constraint is imposed ($\varepsilon=\infty$). In particular, identify conditions on the client distributions $\{\mathcal{P}_k\}$ under which increasing diversity provably reduces $F(h_\theta)$, and conditions under which it cannot.

(b) Characterize, for fixed diversity, the joint feasible region of triples $(U(h_\theta),F(h_\theta),\varepsilon)$ under $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP federated training with clipping parameter $C$ and noise scale $\sigma$. Quantify how decreasing $\varepsilon$ (stronger privacy) degrades $F$ and $U$, including the role of clipping in introducing disparate impact across groups $a\in\mathcal{A}$.

(c) Determine whether the fairness gains attributable to increased diversity can be preserved under non-trivial DP guarantees, or whether DP necessarily erases these gains; provide either an algorithm achieving such preservation with explicit rates, or an impossibility result.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2023–2025) consistently describe the interplay among diversity, fairness, differential privacy, and utility in federated learning as an active open research area. Authors note an inherent tension between DP mechanisms (clipping and noise) and fairness, and a lack of unified theory simultaneously addressing privacy, fairness, and performance. While partial algorithmic progress exists (e.g., zero-sum formulations and DP-fair methods), a comprehensive quantitative characterization remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Privacy and Fairness in Federated Learning: On the Perspective of Tradeoff
status_evidence.snippet: Privacy and fairness compete, and considering each in isolation will inevitably come at the cost of the other.
status_evidence.claim: The privacy–fairness tradeoff in federated learning is an active and unresolved research direction.

status_evidence.title: Mitigating Unfairness in Differentially-Private Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: There is an inherent tradeoff between gradient clipping and noise addition within the DP mechanism when addressing unfairness.
status_evidence.claim: DP mechanisms (clipping/noise) interact with fairness in ways that are still being characterized.

status_evidence.title: Fairness and Privacy-Preserving in Federated Learning: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Existing studies concentrate on privacy, fairness, and robustness separately; unifying their interplay remains significant and open.
status_evidence.claim: A unified analysis of diversity, fairness, and DP in FL is identified as an open problem.
